World.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
World.summary: Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’ Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago. Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville. Sports.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
Sports.summary: As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike. So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson. Continue reading...

Culture.summary: Film-maker Poppy Jay meets a woman who uses her kids for money-making content and another who treats her husband like Jesus. You just wish for even more interrogation – and for a therapist to step in Like film-maker and journalist Poppy Jay’s previous (excellent) documentary, Young, British and Anti-Abortion , her latest offering should come with a warning and blood pressure medication for all women watching. Some men, too, I’m sure, but you’ll forgive me if I can’t quantify the proportion. In Young, British and Tradwife, Jay interviews three women in the UK who are advocating the lifestyle that first took off as a social media phenomenon in the US (where the evangelical Christianity and social conservatism with which it is enmeshed are stronger influences than here). Each of the trio has been chosen with care and balance to represent slightly different manifestations of the movement. Continue reading...

Culture.title: I Am Helen review – Nicola Coughlan is absolutely superb in this terrifying must-watch
Culture.summary: After the week we’ve had, you may not feel ready to watch this brilliantly powerful film about the toxic manosphere and its impact on relationships. But do make the time I would understand, after the week in the news we’ve had, if you were not feeling quite ready to deal with the new instalment of I Am … , Dominic Savage’s anthology series that examines different aspects of women’s lives and tends to do so with merciless precision and in pitiless detail. The stories are worked out with the female actor central to each: Vicky McClure in 2019’s inaugural I Am Nicola, about coercive control, Samantha Morton in one about the vulnerabilities poverty brings, Suranne Jones imploding under the accumulated pressures of midlife and trying to be everything to everyone because nobody else will pick up the slack, and other heavy hitters like Lesley Manville and Kate Winslet starring with younger actors to showcase different generational concerns. The latest was devised with Nicola Coughlan. Continue reading...
